text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming The Game of Life Game I bought this game because of my fond memories of playing as a kid. I gotta tell you, I'm so disappointed by the changes. It's just annoying, every turn can last forever, and I constantly had to be checking the instructions to see what we have to do now, there are so many places where the players each have to stop, and then you need to do a whole bunch of things till it's the next persons turn. For example you stop at graduation, then pick from the cards of jobs. Then you spin again, and then if you pass payday you need to get paid, and then if you land on the action square you need to pick a card and follow directions, sometimes involving one or more players and spinning etc. so a single turn can last five minutes, while all the other players twiddle their thumbs and annoy their mom.
if it sounds confusing, that's because it is. The banker can barely keep up, paydays every minute, there's also a bonus that if someone spins your number they need to pay you, who can keep track when there is so much going on?? They made this game too darn annoying. It was better when it was simpler.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming The Game of Life Game

text_fidelity_a:
Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+ At the time of this review, this set is under $10. If it were over $10, I would probably subtract a star. This is definitely beginner, student quality.
But if you have a child, or maybe you are just looking for something reasonably priced to see if you enjoy sketching, even though it's geared for children, this set can't be beat.

The main reason it gets five stars, is that you get four different hardness levels of graphite pencils. Perfect for experimenting with your creativity and making a sketch come alive. And it's less messy than charcoal sticks, so once again, it's the perfect introduction to nurture a child's creativity and talent.
To make it even better, there's a little pamphlet to encourage and explain how to get your feet wet. I really like that the emphasis is on the fact that there are no mistakes, that each line is is just fine. So important for children that might be discouraged that they aren't instantly a great artist, forgetting or not understanding that being an artist is only 10% talent and 90% learning and desire.
It might be only a folded over page, but it covers various techniques. All is written in a way that kids and young adults can easily follow. This set is cured for ages 7 and up.
And once again, a 7-year-old doesn't need professional quality pencil sharpeners or paper. You can see in the photograph how thin the paper pages are, and how cheesy the little pencil sharpener is. Cheesy, but perfect for the purpose.

This well thought out set is just what I would expect from Farber-Castell. Their supplies are favored by the students and professionals worldwide.

I hope that this review has helped you to make a decision about whether or not this set is right for you or a special child. Kids seem to be passionate about something one minute, and totally change the next. This little set is a very small investment, but of course, little investments add up.

xxoo
text_fidelity_b: Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+

text_fidelity_a:
Pass the Stache Board Game This is definitely not a cerebral or strategizing game. It is pure reaction, action, and laughter. We played a number of rounds as a way to break the ice between to families of children who had not met yet, and it was perfect. The rules are as simple as you can get, flip a card up, if it matches the color or shape of your mustache, hit it with your suction cupped mustache and claim the card. It you suction cup up one that doesn't match, you pay a two card penalty and he who ends with the most cards wins. Ok there are a couple more rules, but that is the gyst. There are also an all smash card and a none smash cards. But seriously, that is the rules right there.

The mustaches themselves are great. They are a blast in themselves as our kids giggled continually at the look of the mustaches touch to everyone's upper lip. They are made strong with decent suction cups below them. It is fairly easy to strike a card and pull it up with the suction cup. And the cards are well made to take the abuse.

As for game play, the rounds are short and exciting. Some feelings got hurt, but for the most part it was an uproarious game which put smiles on everyone's face. Scoring is easy...just count up the cards you won. Personally, I don't think this will be a classic game, but it willl be pulled out in our house many times.
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version Kids like to do grown- up things and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera allows them to do just that. This is a fully- functioning camera specifically designed for the needs and desires of youngsters and it allows kids to take pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even upload them to a computer for further viewing and editing.

Many qualities make this camera one to consider and the first is the memory. This is sold as a child's camera, but it has a surprisingly high level of memory and is capable of holding up to 400 pictures! This is much better than I expected and with this much memory, it will take a long time before kids exceed the available space. They can walk around the house ansd snap picture after picture without worrying that the memory will fill.

Another positive aspect with the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is its durability. This camera is made from plastic with a rubberized edge that makes it easy to hold and highly resistant to breakage. My girls have dropped it several times and it continues to work regardless. It is also very entertaining. Not only can kids take their own pictures of mom, dad, the family dog, and their friends, but they can also add to the fun by using the editing feature. The silly editing allows kids a chance to take an ordinary picture and make it look funny.

So, the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is fun for kids, but are there any cons? Well, there are a few but they are minor enough to overlook. One is the viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is quite small and some images will be barely perceptible. It would be completely unacceptable to adults, but kids will likely find it perfectly fine. Then, one has to consider the picture quality. This camera has only 0.3 megapixels and that means the clarity of the pictures is well below average. Once again, kids are not likely to care. They will so enjoy having their own camera and taking their own pictures that they won't even notice or mind the fuzzy images.

Kids like to mimic adults and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is likely to be a hit with most youngsters for this and other reasons. As I said, the clarity of the photos isn't the best and the camera does have a few other minor flaws, but none of this will matter to most children. The ability to take their own pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even view them on a computer will be more than enough to please the young camerabug in your home.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version

Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets This word game is for 3 – 5 players. It’s for ages 10 and up. Takes 30-minutes to play.

It comes in a cardboard box measuring just under 10” X 6.25” X 2.25”. It’s part of the United States Playing Card company, which makes Bicycle playing cards. Made in China.

Each player receives chips, totaling 30-points, to start. You also receive two cards. From there you go around and each person “pays” for additional cards. Cards with letters which are worth more. . . cost more. You go around four-times. At the end, everyone turns-over their cards and you have thirty-seconds to spell a word with the most points. Please Note: Timer not included. Whomever wins that round gets chips equaling the number of points for their winning word. Then the second place person receives chips worth their number and so on. After playing three times, the person with the most points wins.

FYI. . . This came was originally going to be called “The World Series of AlphaBets”. . . but somewhere along the way they changed it to “Fumbling Ferrets”, probably to make it sound more “family friendly”. But it has nothing to do with ferrets.

If you like word / spelling games, then this one is fairly easy and fast to play. If you’re playing with younger kids, especially to start, you may wish to extend the timer to come-up with a word by a little bit and then shorten it with each round.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor My first introduction to the board game of Sorry was in the early 60's. Sorry was one of the more fast and fun games. The object of the game is to be the first player to move all 4 of your men around the board to get back home. You choose from 4 different colors of your men and your home- blue, green, yellow or red. There is a deck of cards that tell you how many spaces to move your man, and of course it isn't as easy as just moving your man as quickly as you can around the board to get home before anyone and win the game. There are obstacles along the way, should a player get to slide, he slides everyone in his way back to start, and no two men can occupy the same space, so someone has to go back to start- Sorry!

I remember when we played with 2 players, the game took about 15-20 minutes, but with 4 players, it took close to half an hour. It's very fast moving and even faster when hardly any players are sent back to start. I really love the look of this classic 1939 Sorry Game- it's a little different from the one we played on in the 60's. Regardless of the look you like, Sorry is a fast and fun game that brings back so many fun memories of when we had 15 minutes to kill before we went bike riding to a picnic on a lovely summer day in 1962. This early version of the game is really a nice one to own and it also comes with other game versions you can play including a Sorry For One, in case you have a few minutes to kill by yourself! Some Classic games never wear out their fast fun and this 5 Star Classic Sorry Board Game is one of them!
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver [[VIDEOID:a47326bb48b328d18558c86fcccc38a1]] THE GOOD:
--------------
* Very high quality. The handle alone is 12.4 ounces.
* USB-C charging port.
* Belt clip included.
* Decorative blade plug is included. This is cool if you just want to display the handle without the blade. You can cap off your handle with this decorative plug.
* Bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap instead of a pommel/coupling.
* Hilt is 1-1/4 inch. This will connect with other 1.25 inch handles to create a duo saber. Another dominant size on the market is a smaller 1 and 1/8th diameter version. This one will not thread onto 1.25 hilts, so to create duo sabers with different brands, be sure the hilts are the same size.
* All the special effects are pretty much standard: Lock up effect, changing colors, steady, pulse, unstable, etc. This version also has quotes. Watch my video to see a demo

THE BAD:
------------
* Pommel or coupling is not included. As mentioned above, bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap. When you remove this speaker cap, the bottom of this hilt will be male. So to create the duo saber, your other saber should have a coupling so that it's female.
* My light saber did not charge properly out the box. When you plug it in to charge, it'll loudly announce, "Charging!" Then the red light will blink slowly. When it is complete, it will say, "READY," and the red light will be stable, no blinking. Chances are you're not going to be present when the saber says READY. But as long as you see the red light is stable and not blinking, then you'll know it's fully charged. My issue was that after 10 hrs of charging, the red light was still blinking slowly, and the saber wouldn't turn on. I contacted customer support and they had a solution ready to go. So this seems like a common problem. I talk about this at the end of my video, so watch it if you have a charging issue. My saber is charging properly now. So the word to describe this saber is, finicky.

I'll give this an overall rating of 4-Stars.
text_fidelity_b: CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver

Crayola Super Tips Washable Markers Age 3+ - 50 Count I'll admit it: I'm an adult who loves to color. I find it a great way to relax, and there are some amazing "coloring books for adults" gaining popularity these days (Johanna Basford, Angie Grace, etc.). And there are whole communities of "colorists" popping up on social media.

So naturally, I'm looking for different mediums to use when I color. I've used colored pencils and gel pens, so I figured it was time to branch out into the marker arena. Someone suggested starting with these as they're water-based rather than alcohol-based, and Amazon has them at a good price, so I got the 50-ct set.

Overall, I'm pleased. There is a good selection of colors, several shades of each, which helps to bring some variety into th mix.

What I DON'T like (and this seems to be a problem for ALL coloring mediums): the actual color of the pen/pencil/etc. almost NEVER matches the color of the cap/barrel/etc. I realize that colors will look different depending on the type a "color" of paper used as the background, but seriously, some of these are WAY off. I find myself having to make a "cheat sheet" on the paper I'm using just so I can get a clear picture of how the various colors REALLY look.

Like I said, this isn't just a problem with Crayola, but they make it a little more difficult because the pens have NO distinguishing markings on them whatsoever to designate a color number or code. I ended up putting little pieces of masking tape on each pen and numbering them myself just so I can keep the color charts coordinated.

All that aside, they work great once you figure out the colors. Colors are vibrant, and I had very little "bleed through" or feathering in an Angie Grace book. Bleed through and feathering depend a great deal on the paper used, so bear that in mind and ALWAYS test before coloring.

Overall​, I like these - don't "love" them, but they're good quality water-based markers at a very good price.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Super Tips Washable Markers Age 3+ - 50 Count

Hot Wheels Toy Car Track Set Hill Climb Champion with 1:64 Scale Car, Launch Uphill to Score Points & Win Amazon was temporarily out of stock so I grabbed this from another source. We are an avid Hot Wheels family and always like to check out the newer sets. I love the idea of running a car around a course continuously, without relying on batteries. This set comes with a big launcher, that features a unique track with protruding tabs that catch the cars from behind as you blast them around the track. The whole idea is to catch the car(s) at the right time when it reenters the launcher, so you can have it racing around the course non-stop. Unfortunately, the course is too small and uninteresting, yet, if the layout was much larger, that launcher wouldn't have enough force without some kind of midway helper (like an automatic loop launcher). This would make a world of a difference in fun, so you you're not pounding the launcher every half second to keep the car circulating around a tiny oval which gets old fast.

Big annoyance: The launcher is very tall, so it comes in packed in two pieces which easily lock together, however, once locked, you're unable to seperate them. This is now the second set we have with this annoying problem. We like storing our hot wheels in their boxes, but once opened, there's no way to get this giant launcher back inside. Even if storing out of the box, with other toys, it's a big jalopy that could have been dismantled, taking up less space.

And finally, kids need laser-sharp hand/eye coordination to catch the car on time, so this may frustrate the impatient type. When you do manage to catch the car to keep it going, it does feel rewarding, even if it's only 2 laps. We haven't tried more than one car at a time, but I imagine on a large course, it must be fun, but on this small circuit, it's probably near impossible to work with.

VELIYAKA Flowers Building Blocks Set, 12 Kits Mini Bonsai Tree Building Toys , Simulation Succulent Flower Building Bricks for Home Decoration,Kids Girls Women Birthday Gifts This is a set of 12 little succulents. The description says 12 and 6, but really, you get 12 sets.

THE GOOD:
🌵 The sets are individually packaged, with their own directions, pieces, and coffee cup container. The box has a picture of the set inside, so if you wanted, you could give a set as a gift. Or if there’s a certain succulent you want to build, you can easily find it.

🌵 The box identifies the succulent. I like knowing the name of what I’m building!

🌵 The sets are quick builds. It took me about 75 minutes to do all 12.

🌵 The instructions are simple, there are a few confusing steps but since these are plants, I was okay with them not being perfect.

🌵 The finished succulents do make cool display pieces, and are a perfect size for desks, bookshelves, or even windowsills. They are small: about 2 inches at the widest point and 5 inches for the tallest.

THE BAD:
🌵 The pieces don’t stay together very well. Some do and some do not. I had several construction accidents while building because some pieces clicked and some did not. Some pieces are very loose, one of the succulents (February, Plum Blossom) fell apart while I was building another.

🌵 I was unable to build one of the succulents because the thing would just not stay together. That was the December set, Antirrhinum majus. The main body of the plant is two pieces that will not snap together.

🌵 My sunflower is missing a petal because the necessary piece was malformed.

🌵 The coffee cup lids are a cute idea, but they did not stay connected to the cups. The lids are intended as the base for each cup, but no matter how hard I tried, the cups popped right off the lids. Fortunately, the cups are stable without needing to sit on the lids.

Overall, while this box of 12 succulents is a good value, I was somewhat disappointed that the succulents didn’t always stay together. A finished set shouldn’t fall apart while it’s sitting on the table because the pieces are loose.

text_fidelity_a:
Cat Construction 15" Toy Excavator , Yellow Note: There are multiple products attached to this listing. I am specifically writing this review for the CAT excavator.

When I received this item I was a bit surprised at how large it is, bigger than I expected. I was thinking this would be approximately the size of a bread loaf pan (a testament to how terrible my sense of measure is), so when the box arrived I was surprised when I opened it to find this large plastic truck.

This truck is all plastic which has some pluses and minuses about it. It’s not all that expensive, which would not be the case if it was metal or had metal parts in it. It’s completely waterproof, and it is made well enough to handle some limited abuse. It is not made of heavy-grade plastic, though, so if it is thrown or stood upon it could break.

There are moving parts but everything is manual. No levers, no buttons, no wheels other than the tires, so play isn’t as automated. This may or may not frustrate a young child, though that depends on the child and not the toy. It’s not a toy for the impatient.

This is a decent toy though there are some trade-offs. For the price it is a good unit that will keep a patient child busy. It is not the sturdiest nor is it the most technologically advanced, so it can be broken if handled very roughly and it may prove frustrating for a child who expects some automation.
text_fidelity_b: Cat Construction 15" Toy Excavator , Yellow

Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover I've answered a few questions about this, so I will include this right away- this is only a plush (a really nice one)- it has no mechanical parts. It doesn't purr, or "breathe", makes no kitten or cat sounds, and therefore, requires no batteries.

This item was purchased as an "emotional support plushie", if you will. People need companionship, even folks who are no longer able to care for a living pet (or no longer wish to have the heartbreak of losing a real cat).

This fellow can absolutely be mistaken for a real cat at a distance. While being held and stroked, it's close enough to pass for a cat who is less than bunny-soft. The expressions and eyes are amazing, the little toe beans are soft silicone and give a little when squeezed. I couldn't have asked for more detail.

The care that went into creating this plush is evident in the details- from the examples in the pictures and video to those included from customer reviews (and those of the custom plushies are OUTSTANDING, I may have to treat myself to one someday!). It comes in a reusable case (resembling a cat carrier) with a little care booklet and grooming tool.

Personally I wouldn't give this plush to a young child (especially not one of the long-haired ones)- frankly, I'd be worried they'd damage it (squish things in the fur, allow the fur to become matted, color it with markers, cut the whiskers or fur...). Kids can be amazingly accidently destructive at times (we know they don't mean to, it just happens).

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.

Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue) I love the old console games and I looked to this handheld to revisit some of the older games I remember enjoying several years ago. For the price this is a decent little console and I like it, though there is some room for improvement.

In the past, playing the older games required downloading a ROM and putting it into an emulator, and if you knew where to look for ROMs you could find hundreds of them, many familiar and even more that were very unfamiliar. I expected this little console to be something silimar to the old emulator, preloaded with old ROMs, and it seems to be fairly close to that. There are many games I recognize that are a lot fo fun to revisit, and there are a lot of games that are unfamiliar.

This console comes preloaded with several hundred games of varying types and quality. As mentioned there are quite a few that are familiar, but many that I never saw in an arcade. Some appear to be Asian releases that never were released here.

Navigation is a minor pain. If you want to play a game that is far down the list, you have to navigate there every time. There doesn't appear to be any memory for last games played.

Another minor disappointment is that several titles are listed more than once in the menu. This suggests to me that there are different versions, even if I can't tell what the differences are.

I'm thinking this is the same thing as the old emulators that can be found online and it just packaged in a handheld and preloaded with ROMs. That's fine by me, I like those old games. It would have been nice to provide better navigation, though, and maybe reduce the versions of each game to the latest or most bug-free? For the cost, it's a worthwhile system if you love those old games.
text_fidelity_b: Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends Wood, Animal Park Set We have almost the entire Thomas and friends Fisher-Price wood set of the new type of connectors, and we do not have any of the old style tracks from any brands. Overall the new tracks stay together very well and are easy to put together, but in all honesty my three-year-old sometimes has to bring these new style wood tracks to me to get them apart, which she never has to do with the tiny set of traditional tracks that grandma has at her house. What is nice is that you can attach the tracks from either direction, since both sides connect identically.

We have the busy island set, the farm set, cranky at the docks, the train station, and the huge Tidwell sheds station. All of these sets fit together beautifully and provide a lot of different play options for the kids. However, the main complaint I have had is that most of these sets have not come with enough tracks. Even the huge sets, come with just enough tracks to barely get it together if you are very careful and mindful with how you put things together.

The main advantage of a set like this animal park one, is that you get a whole lot of tracks and every piece in it can be used to connect all of the big and exciting things in those huge sets. My daughter also really loved the simplicity of this set, that she doesn't really have to think too hard about how it goes together, she can just wind and turn and connect things up without too much planning ahead.

Overall this set adds to the larger Thomas sets really nicely and is a great way of introducing a little more interest and a lot more tracks into the busy island set or another one of the bigger sets.
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends Wood, Animal Park Set

text_fidelity_a:
Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor This is one of those toys that can provide HOURS of entertainment AND education. You're working those brain cells to build these railways! There's a booklet included with lots of different railways to build. It gives you step by step instructions by picture. You DO have to pay close attention to what color block you place where, and where the holes line up, and how many blocks you use. It all has to line up just right. That said, I wouldn't call this a difficult toy at all. It *will* exercise the mind, though.

I like using it with my 5 year old. It's helping him to follow directions. Of course, I still have to help a great deal. It's also helping him with counting, which he struggles with. It's helping my 2 year old learn his colors. Plus, we're ALL learning patience! ;) These railways fall down pretty easily, since it's basically stacking blocks on top of each other. Honestly, for most 2-3 year olds, I think this thing probably isn't the best idea just yet. For older children, it's wonderful. It has potential to grow with them for *years* to come. This is fun for adults, too! I've had a blast with it.

My ONLY complaint with this thing is the fact that the marbles have nothing to catch them as the come out of the final holes/blocks. They just roll away. We have a 7 month old that crawls everywhere and puts everything in his mouth. We're always careful, but playing with this thing, we have to be extraordinarily careful, especially due to the free rolling marble issue. So far, we haven't came up with a "catching place" for those last marbles, but I'm sure we will in time. We just can't use all the marbles at one time, and keep a close count on what we do use.

The extra caution we have to use is WELL worth it, though!!

This is the kind of toy you just can't go wrong with! (Unless you have children that might choke on those marbles...use your best judgment at that point). Highly recommended from us!
text_fidelity_b: Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor

Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces) The Mega Construx Kadabra is better suited for display rather than actual play. His hands fall off quite easily. The play feature of the purple orb is pretty meh. But due to his ball and socket joints, he stands without needing assistance or to lean against anything.

Assembly takes about 30 minutes. The instructions are clear; the hardest part is often clicking the pieces together. My fingers actually hurt after I was finished, due to the pressure I needed to exert to get some of the pieces to fit together. I’ve noticed this with other Mega Construx sets. I wish they would fix this, as it makes it harder for young kids to do this on their own.

The set is rated 6+, which I would say is accurate for the instructions and building. The main difficulty will be snapping pieces together. I had imprints on my fingers -- that’s how hard it can be to get some pieces to fit. Which is ironic, considering how easily some other pieces, like Kadabra’s hands, fall off the finished Pokémon.

The printing on his face and chest is a lighter pink than it appears on the box.

The moustache fur is made of a floppy plastic, so it does move around when the figure is moved. This was probably my favorite part of the set, as I thought it added character to the Kadabra. A little piece of advice: I recommend fitting the moustache around the knob of the piece meant to secure it, putting it together upside down instead of the way the instructions show. This way you can ensure it’s evenly lined up.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces)

The dashboard has very little room to put things in when it's open, and the angle is such that things really don't stay put very well at the dashboard is open, so I would've liked a little bit better design on that, because my kids had to work hard to find something they wanted to bring along that was small enough to fit. The trunk is also a little small and again the shape of the interior of it makes it harder for things to fit in, because it is just a rectangular box opening that is kind of slick, so when you put things in the kind of want to slide out. There is enough room in the car to where they could have made the trunk much more substantial, and it would've made this an even cooler car.

That said, these are just quibbles and the real proof of whether a toy is any good is in the pudding. My kids love it, and they've been playing with it nonstop and vrooming the girls around on all kinds of adventures since the car arrived. I've been delighted to see the amount of imaginative play that has taken place with the addition of a car, to where the girls can leave the bedroom and go on all kinds of fun adventures.

The car seems well-made and is very sturdy, the doors open, and if you need to put the windshield down for storage, it does fold down. Overall this is a great toy if you have 14 inch dolls who need some adventure in their lives.
